title: Other Pay Added to the Waiver Income Count — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Training Bulletin
content:
Other pay reported on certified weeks ending in the income window is added to the countable annual income on a Benefit Overpayment Accounts waiver request. The certified weeks are the weekly certifications on the claimant's Unemployment Benefit Claims whose week ending Saturday falls in the three whole months before the handling date (whole months from the week ending date to the handling date fewer than 3); the other pay is the kind and amount of other pay reported on them.

| Other pay reported in the income window | Amount added |
|---|---|
| A pension | For each kind of pension reported, employer-funded and claimant-contributed, the latest weekly amount reported in the income window; the amounts for the kinds reported are added up and multiplied by 52, the weeks in a year |
| No pension, but vacation pay or holiday pay | The vacation and holiday pay reported in the window, added once, at the amounts reported |
| Neither a pension nor vacation or holiday pay | Nothing |

## Questions answered

**A claimant reported an employer-funded pension of USD 90.00 a week on earlier weeks and USD 100.00 a week on the latest week in the window. Which amount is used?** The latest weekly amount reported, USD 100.00.

**If both kinds of pension are reported?** The latest weekly amount of each kind is taken and the two are added: USD 100.00 employer-funded and USD 40.00 claimant-contributed give USD 140.00, multiplied by 52, USD 7,280.00 added.

**Vacation pay of USD 300.00 and holiday pay of USD 120.00 are reported in the window, with no pension. What is added?** USD 420.00, once.

**A pension and vacation pay are both reported?** Only the pension row applies; the vacation pay is not added.

**Only severance pay is reported?** Nothing is added; neither a pension nor vacation or holiday pay is reported.
